template.title: Info event
template.card: A talk or meetup for your members and people who might join, from first plan to follow-up.
guidance: Goal: more people in your town who see why a pause is needed and possible, some of them joining your group, and a format you can repeat.
One ask runs through everything: join the chat group, come to the next meeting, take a task. Decide it in Plan the event; title, talk and promotion then point at it.
The event is a recruiting conversation with a talk in the middle, not a lecture. Small and full beats big and empty: 15–30 people, three to four weeks of lead time.
Start with Plan the event; once goal, date and speaker are fixed, Location, Give a good talk and Promote the event run in parallel. Give every sub-project an owner; don't do it alone.
You are responsible for the room; the [code of conduct](https://pauseai.info/code-of-conduct) and the [safeguarding protocol](https://pauseai.info/safeguarding-protocol) say what that means.
Resources: [Running a local PauseAI community](https://pauseai.info/local-organizing)

children.title: Plan the event
guidance: Goal: decide what everything else depends on — purpose, format, date and speaker — before anyone books a room or posts a link.

One event, one goal: a first meeting for people who might join, or a talk plus an action session where attendees act on the spot. Title, talk and ask all serve it; if you want members, leave more time for talking than for slides. For a first event, you or a co-organizer speak; an outside speaker once you have run one.
The result is one paragraph with numbers that every other sub-project works from. Event formats and sample agendas: [Running a local PauseAI community](https://pauseai.info/local-organizing).

children.title: Decide the goal and the ask
children.hint: One sentence: who should come, and what they should do at the end — join the chat, come again, take a task.

children.title: Choose the format
children.hint: Talk, questions, mingling; or a screening with a short intro and the same ask. 90 minutes is enough; a third of it for talking.

children.title: Set the date
children.hint: Three to four weeks ahead; check for clashes with local events your audience goes to; confirm with your co-organizers.

children.title: Confirm the speaker
children.hint: You or a co-organizer for a first event; agree length and message; put a rehearsal date in the calendar.

children.title: Set targets
children.hint: Numbers make it real: attendees, contacts collected, people at the next meeting. You compare against them in Follow-up.

children.summary: goal, format, date, speaker; everything else depends on these.

children.title: Location
guidance: Goal: a free room for 15–30 people that is easy to find, booked as soon as the date is set.

Public libraries, community centers, university rooms, cafés and bookshops off-peak, town halls and churches lend rooms to community groups for free if you ask early; in a café, people are expected to buy something. Reachable by public transport in the evening, step-free if possible; a circle of chairs in a small room beats a half-empty lecture hall.

Directions beyond the street address — floor, room, how to get in — and a sign on the door; people who can't find you go home. Leave the room as you found it and thank the host; you will want it again. More venue ideas: [Running a local PauseAI community](https://pauseai.info/local-organizing).

children.title: Shortlist three venues
children.hint: Library, community center, university room, café off-peak; free for community groups if you ask early; note capacity and closing time.

children.title: Book the room
children.hint: Confirm date, slot with 30 minutes setup, projector and chairs; get the booking in writing.

children.title: Check the room
children.hint: Visit or ask for photos: entrance, screen, sound, power; decide where the sign-up sheet sits.

children.title: Write the directions
children.hint: Floor, room, how to get in after hours, a phone number; the same text goes on Luma and on the door sign.

children.title: (optional) Arrange drinks and snacks
children.hint: Simple and cheap; people stay and talk longer with something in their hands; ask the venue what is allowed.

children.summary: a free room for 15–30 people, booked early.

children.title: Give a good talk
guidance: Goal: twenty minutes after which the room sees why a pause is needed and possible, and wants to help.

Follow the PauseAI pitch structure: your story, the problem, the solution (a pause), how we get there, why now, what to do tonight. Take claims from [Core positions](https://pauseai-global.notion.site/Core-Positions-105bbc7720194fa29029dbf12e0ee96d) and cite experts and sources, not opinions: nonpartisan, no jargon, honest about uncertainty.

Pair every warning with a way to act; people move when they believe the risk is real and a pause achievable. Tailor the problem section to the room — students, a climate group, the public. Ten slides at most; the conversation afterwards matters more than the slides. In questions, acknowledge concerns and say what we know; don't try to win every argument.
The pitch structure in full: [Running a local PauseAI community](https://pauseai.info/local-organizing).

children.title: Write the outline
children.hint: Six parts: your story, the problem, the pause, how we get there, why now, the ask; one line each before any slide.

children.title: Check claims against Core positions
children.hint: Use the ten agreed lines and their sources; cut what you can't source; no party politics, no jargon.

children.title: Make the slides
children.hint: Ten at most, big text, a source under every number; the slide format of the [Collateral maker](https://pauseai.uk/tools/collateral) gives an on-brand title slide.

children.title: Prepare for questions
children.hint: List the five questions you expect and one honest answer each, starting from the [FAQ](https://pauseai.info/faq) and [Counterarguments](https://pauseai.info/counterarguments); where you don't know, say so.

children.title: Rehearse once, timed
children.hint: Out loud, with slides, in front of a co-organizer; cut until it's 20 minutes; ask what they'd repeat to a friend.

children.summary: twenty minutes on why a pause is needed and possible.

children.title: Promote the event
guidance: Goal: the right people in the room — members, their friends, and people from nearby groups.

Say what happens, when, where and for whom; nobody comes to a vague event. The Luma event is the one link everything else points at. A direct ask with a date beats any post, so each organizer invites people personally.

Public posts carry the PauseAI name: nonpartisan, no jargon, verified claims. Check wording against [How we do messaging](https://app.notion.com/p/pauseai-global/How-we-do-messaging-3758114391768082b456d3a51e688e41) (members) and run unsure drafts through the [Comms checker prompt](https://app.notion.com/p/pauseai-global/Comms-checker-prompt-3ac81143917680cc8449f53877606b3c) (members). Images come from the [Collateral maker](https://pauseai.uk/tools/collateral): its Event layout makes an on-brand post, Luma cover or flyer from a form.
Post twice, two weeks before and the day before, and remind sign-ups the day before; many forget.

children.title: Create the Luma event
children.hint: Title, time, place with directions, three lines on what happens and for whom; submit it to the [PauseAI calendar](https://luma.com/PauseAI) so subscribers get notified.

children.title: Post on Instagram
children.hint: Make the image with the [Collateral maker](https://pauseai.uk/tools/collateral): Event layout, your details, download; post two weeks before and again the day before.

children.title: Share in other local communities
children.hint: Uni groups, meetups, climate and effective altruism groups: a short personal message with the link and why their members might care.

children.title: Invite people personally
children.hint: Each organizer asks five people directly, with the date: friends, classmates, coworkers. Direct asks bring more people than any post.

children.title: (optional) Print flyers
children.hint: [Collateral maker](https://pauseai.uk/tools/collateral), A6 or A5 format, about 100 copies; hand out on campus or downtown a week before; see the [Flyering guide](https://pauseai.info/flyering).

children.title: Remind sign-ups the day before
children.hint: A short Luma message: time, directions, what to expect. Many sign-ups forget; a reminder is the cheapest way to fill the room.

children.summary: the right people in the room: members, their friends, nearby groups.

children.title: At the event
guidance: Goal: everyone leaves with a next step and you with their contact — a recruiting conversation, not a lecture.

Run it like PauseAI's teach-ins: mingling, the talk, a short action everyone does together, the invitation to get involved. In the breaks, ask newcomers what brought them and what they'd like to do; giving some of them a small role on the day brings them back.

Safeguarding is your job: the reporting contact visible, nobody alone with a minor, and you know how to handle a disclosure; the [safeguarding protocol](https://pauseai.info/safeguarding-protocol) has the event checklist. Collect name, email and what they'd help with; contacts belong in your chapter's list, not your phone.
The teach-in agenda: [Running a local PauseAI community](https://pauseai.info/local-organizing).

children.title: Prepare sign-up sheet and QR code
children.hint: Name, email, "I'd like to help with…"; a QR code to the chat group invite; one sheet per table, pens.

children.title: Assign roles for the day
children.hint: Door and directions, sign-ups, photos, timekeeper, someone whose job is talking to newcomers; ask a new member to take one.

children.title: Run the safeguarding checklist
children.hint: Contact safeguarding@pauseai.info on a slide and the door sign; code of conduct on Luma; parental consent for under-18s; the [event checklist](https://pauseai.info/safeguarding-protocol#14-event-operations-checklist) has the rest.

children.title: Plan the action session
children.hint: Ten minutes where everyone does something: write to their representative with the [Email builder](https://pauseai.info/email-builder), join the chat, sign up for a task; prepare the materials.

children.title: Make the ask and name the next date
children.hint: Join the chat now, next meeting on a date you announce, one task per volunteer; say it before questions and again last.

children.title: (optional) Take photos
children.hint: A few wide shots of a full room for the follow-up post; ask before posting faces.

children.summary: a recruiting conversation, not a lecture; everyone leaves with a next step.

children.title: Follow-up
guidance: Goal: turn the evening into members — within two days everyone who came hears from you with one thing to do.

Interest fades within days; a week later is too late. Ask for something small and specific; "let us know if you want to help" gets no replies. A one-on-one with everyone who ticked "I'd like to help" is where roles are agreed: what brought them, how much time they have, a first task.

Numbers against the targets from Plan the event tell you what to change. Recruiting continuously beats one burst, and the people you just met need somewhere to go next — the next date. One-on-ones and continuous recruitment: [Running a local PauseAI community](https://pauseai.info/local-organizing).

children.title: Message everyone who came
children.hint: Within two days: thanks, chat invite, next meeting date, one concrete thing to do this week. Short and personal.

children.title: Hold one-on-ones with interested people
children.hint: 20–30 minutes each: what brought them, what they'd like to do, how much time; leave with a role and a first task.

children.title: Post the photos
children.hint: A few photos and two lines on how it went; tag the chapter; thank venue and speaker publicly.

children.title: Record the numbers
children.hint: Attendees, contacts, how many came again; one line on what to change next time; share it with your chapter.

children.title: Set the next date
children.hint: Announce the next meeting while the event is fresh; the people you just met need somewhere to go.

children.summary: within two days, everyone who came hears from you.

comingSoon.title: Protest
comingSoon.description: A peaceful public protest or creative action that gets attention from passers-by, journalists and decision-makers: place and date, signs and flyers, a press release and media invites, roles for the day, speeches and chants prepared in advance. Built on the guide to organizing a PauseAI protest, with the legal part for your country.

comingSoon.title: Coalition building
comingSoon.description: Reach the people around you with influence or reach: local politicians, journalists, other groups, and the well-connected. One owner per contact, a good first email and notes on how to talk to them, sent and tracked through the outreach pipeline; for groups with committed volunteers.
